g.text: What a watermark is — a monotonic claim about completeness
perfect watermark stalls at 12:00:50 for 6 events · heuristic reaches 12:03:05 and publishes 15 instead of 19

EVENT TIME VS WATERMARK, EVENT BY EVENT
row 1 = the arriving event · row 2 = its event time · row 3 = the watermark after it (max seen − lag)

The highlighted event times go BACKWARDS — id 6 at 12:03:40 after id 5 at 12:04:20, then id 7 at 12:00:50.
The watermark row never does. It is monotonically increasing by construction, because it is computed from the MAXIMUM event time seen, not from
the latest one.
Step 1/4 — event times jump around; the watermark only moves forward
A watermark is a single event-time value that only ever moves forward. Compare the two bottom rows: event times arrive out of order 2 times, and
the watermark still never decreases. That is not luck — `max(seen)` cannot shrink, and monotonicity is what lets a window be closed once rather
than re-opened.
What a watermark is — a monotonic claim about completeness
perfect watermark stalls at 12:00:50 for 6 events · heuristic reaches 12:03:05 and publishes 15 instead of 19
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · lag 60s · window [12:00, 12:02) = 19
WHAT THE WATERMARK ACTUALLY ASSERTS
one value, and the four different things people read into it
watermark = 12:03:05 after event id 4
the claim: "nothing earlier than 12:03:05 will arrive"
the wall clock at that moment
12:04:06 — a different number, about a different thing
what the claim allows
every window ending at or before 12:03:05 may now be emitted
whether the claim is TRUE here
no — id 7 (12:00:50) has not arrived yet
A watermark is a PROMISE the pipeline makes so that triggers have something to fire on. It is not a guarantee and it is not the wall clock.
Here the promise is false at the moment it is made, and nothing in the pipeline can tell. That is the normal condition, not a malfunction.
Step 2/4 — it is a claim about completeness, not a clock reading
Two numbers exist at that instant: the watermark (12:03:05, in event time) and the wall clock (12:04:06, in processing time). They are not
comparable — one is a claim about which events can still arrive, the other is what time it is. The claim here is wrong, which is why "estimate"
rather than "guarantee" is the word that matters.
What a watermark is — a monotonic claim about completeness
perfect watermark stalls at 12:00:50 for 6 events · heuristic reaches 12:03:05 and publishes 15 instead of 19

PERFECT VS HEURISTIC, SIDE BY SIDE
the perfect watermark is the largest time for which no earlier event is still to come — computable only in hindsight

id 1

none yet

everything
heuristic (row 2) advances to 12:03:05 by event id 4 · perfect (row 3) is stuck at 12:00:50
The perfect watermark cannot pass 12:00:50 for 6 consecutive events, because id 7 (12:00:50) is still to come.
The heuristic advanced to 12:03:05 in that same span. It bought 135s of apparent progress by being wrong.
Step 3/4 — a PERFECT watermark exists — and it stalls
This is the clearest statement of what a heuristic watermark is FOR. The perfect watermark is correct and useless — it sits at 12:00:50 for 6 of
the 9 events, so nothing can be emitted. The heuristic reaches 12:03:05 in the same span, and every bit of that 135s of progress is an unverified
guess.
What a watermark is — a monotonic claim about completeness
perfect watermark stalls at 12:00:50 for 6 events · heuristic reaches 12:03:05 and publishes 15 instead of 19
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · lag 60s · window [12:00, 12:02) = 19
THE SAME WINDOW, UNDER BOTH WATERMARKS
perfect and heuristic differ in exactly one way: latency versus truth
ids 0, 1, 2, 7 · true sum 19
heuristic: closes after event id 4
publishes 15 at 12:04:06 — 21% low
perfect: closes after event id 7
publishes 19 at 12:04:40 — correct
the price of being right
34s later, and it required knowing the future
The perfect watermark gives 19 because it refused to claim completeness until id 7 had actually landed.
It could only do that because this generator can read the whole stream. A live pipeline cannot, so a heuristic is not a shortcut — it is the only
option.
Step 4/4 — and that is exactly the price of the on-time answer
Both watermarks drive the same on-time trigger, and the window's answer differs: 15 at 12:04:06 against 19 at 12:04:40. 34s buys 4 of the 19. And
the perfect version is not a design option: it required looking at events that had not arrived.
